knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes Normal-approximation confidence intervals for a binomial probability and a Poisson mean?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the dual binomial-p and Poisson-mean claim.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Both single-sample binomial-p and Poisson-mean intervals appear, with Normal approximation where appropriate. They are not the same formula, and two-sample contrasts are a different setting.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Binomial-p and Poisson-mean CIs, with Normal approximation when appropriate.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Covering only one discrete model, or swapping in two-sample formulas.

choices.label: Form a CI for a binomial probability p and a CI for a Poisson mean λ, using a Normal approximation (with the appropriate variance function) when that approximation is justified.
A binomial CI for p is enough; the Poisson mean uses the identical formula after renaming p as λ, including the p(1−p) variance.
Normal approximation is never used for discrete data; only exact binomial or Poisson intervals are allowed.
Two-sample difference intervals replace single-sample binomial and Poisson intervals in this setting.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly gives Normal-approximation CI forms for a binomial probability and a Poisson mean (single sample)?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bernoulli variance is p(1−p)/n; Poisson mean variance is λ/n (per observation in the usual sample-mean form). Swapping those variance functions, or dropping Poisson entirely, is wrong.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: p̂ ± z√(p̂(1−p̂)/n) and λ̂ ± z√(λ̂/n); both required.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reusing Bernoulli variance for Poisson, or treating one discrete CI as enough.

choices.label: Binomial: p̂ ± z_{1−α/2} √(p̂(1−p̂)/n). Poisson: λ̂ ± z_{1−α/2} √(λ̂/n) (or an equivalent total-count form with matching variance). Both are required; one does not replace the other.
Binomial: p̂ ± z_{1−α/2} √(p̂(1−p̂)/n). The Poisson interval is the same expression with λ̂ written in place of p̂ and with variance p̂(1−p̂)/n kept unchanged.
Binomial: p̂ ± z_{1−α/2} √(p̂/n). Poisson: λ̂ ± z_{1−α/2} √(λ̂(1−λ̂)/n).
Only the binomial form is required; Poisson means are handled by transforming to a Normal mean interval for x̄ with variance s²/n from continuous data.
